question: What is the SI unit of mass?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kilogram**__.

__
 
• The **kilogram** is the SI unit of **mass**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• It is one of the fundamental quantities in Physics and the most basic property of matter.
 
• We can define **mass **as the measure of the amount of matter in a body.
 
• The **mass of a body does not change at any time.**
 
• Only for certain extreme cases when a huge amount of energy is given or taken from a body.
 
• For example: in a nuclear reaction, a tiny amount of matter is converted into a huge amount of energy, this reduces the mass of the substance.
 
• **Mass** is a **scalar quantity, **It has magnitude.
 
• **Mass can never be zero.**
 
• Relation Between Weight and Mass
 
 
• If an object with a mass of 1kg falls with an acceleration of 9.8 m.s⁻², then the magnitude of the force is given as
 
• **F = ma**

 = (1 kg)(9.8 m.s⁻²)

 = (9.8 kg.m.s⁻²)

 = 9.8N
